title: A person installs nocx with one brew command from our own tap, and it opens without a manual quarantine step
description:
Owner's decision, 2026-09-30: nocx is published through our own Homebrew tap as a
cask. This reverses the "Homebrew stays closed" statements of ADR-0003 and
ADR-0052, which read the 2026-09-01 rule as closing every tap.

## Why the ADRs were wrong about taps

The 2026-09-01 Gatekeeper rule disables unsigned casks in the official
`homebrew/cask` only. A Homebrew maintainer, in
https://github.com/orgs/Homebrew/discussions/6482: "Anyone can create their own
Tap and add whatever they'd like to it. By default, we don't even check signing
status on third-party taps." `brew` still quarantines what it downloads, and a
tap cask clears that in a post-install step (`postflight_steps` in Homebrew 6;
raw `postflight` is deprecated). Taps doing exactly this exist
(thedavidweng/homebrew-unsigned-tap). None of this is measured on a Mac yet.

## What it involves

- A new ADR superseding the Homebrew statements of ADR-0003 and ADR-0052 (never
  edit them); `docs/vision.md` §8 and the README install section follow it.
- A tap repository `shady2k/homebrew-nocx` with cask `nocx`: `auto_updates true`,
  because the app updates itself through the ed25519-signed manifest and `brew
  upgrade` must not fight it; a post-install step removing
  `com.apple.quarantine` from `/Applications/nocx.app`; a README stating plainly
  that the tap strips quarantine.
- A `release.yml` step that updates version and sha256 in the tap after a
  release publishes, with a token scoped to the tap repository only.
- The bundle is the same one: ADR-0052's code identity is untouched.

## DONE WHEN

On a clean macOS, `brew install --cask shady2k/nocx/nocx` installs nocx, it
launches without the Gatekeeper dialog and without a manual `xattr`, and after
the next release the in-app update succeeds and a following `brew upgrade`
neither reinstalls nor downgrades it. A manual pass on a Mac, recorded on this
epic — there is no macOS e2e runner. Disproved by any Gatekeeper prompt on first
launch, or by `brew` refusing the cask.

## Out

- The official `homebrew/cask` tap: it needs notarization, and there is no
  Developer ID (ADR-0003 stands on that).
- A formula building from source: a locally built bundle is not signed with the
  project certificate, which breaks ADR-0052's keychain identity.
- Linux packages via brew (the Linux channel is nocx-j3prm).

title: The bounded live tier punches visible holes in the durable record's capture
description:
## What a stranger can check

- main (394b27a68): `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/transcript-scroll-budget.spec.ts` — passes (2.9m).
- stage branch before the surface (5a3f86b4b) and at PR #260 head: the same spec fails — first at block 105 with the DEFAULT budget, at block 290 with `terminal.scrollbackLines = 100000`.

## Root cause

nocx-zg3k3.10.1 bounded the live tier: every session now carries `terminal.scrollbackLines` (default 10,000) and the port ALWAYS applies a 32 MiB per-session memory ceiling (internal/emulator/ghostty/scrollback.go:38, "raising it is a separate change behind that same measurement"). On main the adapter CLEARED both limits — that unbounded world was load-bearing for the durable record's capture: block rows are read from the emulator's departure report, and when the library prunes pages inside one feed, the feed's own departures and the pruned pages are one count no scalar separates (ADR-0075's hole), so the block freezes INCOMPLETE with "Output incomplete: output was lost once before it could be captured" — honest per the port's contract, and the transcript spec's freeze wait (which requires the command's first row) starves.

Numbers: the spec's 500 blocks need ~50,000 rows ≈ 70 MiB at its pane width (~148 cols × 9.75 B/row). The default 10k binds at block ~105; the line maximum 100,000 cannot help because 32 MiB binds at ~29k rows there. No setting value reaches the premise.

## The decision (owner)

1. Raise `scrollbackMaxBytes` behind the measurement the port's comment demands — keeps capture complete for high-volume sessions, spends memory the guard rail exists to bound (AD-10's aggregate).
2. Decouple block capture from live retention — the durable record keeps every row regardless of the live tier's bounds. Real architecture work (the departure read is the seam; nocx-zg3k3.5 territory).
3. Accept bounded capture with visible incomplete marks, and adapt the record's consumers — the transcript spec would shrink to fit inside the guard rail, and the product promise about blocks becomes "complete up to the live budget".

Filed by the stage coordinator at the zg3k3.10 PR: CI is red on ci-e2e shard 2 (both browsers) because of this, and the PR cannot merge until the owner picks.

comments.author: omp-coordinator
comments.text: blocked: owner decision between three options (raise the 32 MiB ceiling behind measurement; decouple capture from live retention; accept bounded capture and adapt consumers). Evidence and commands in the description; reproducible on PR #260's branch.

comments.author: omp-coordinator
comments.text:
Consultation round (codex, two passes over the tree):

DIRECTION CONFIRMED — decouple durable capture from live retention (option 2): a monotonic departure odometer + retained floor/generation + a departure journal in the fork's ABI, captured at the primary active-area boundary crossing (BEFORE retention/discard — zero retention erases immediately, so hooking history-append is insufficient). Marker/block attribution stays in Go (ADR-0024 authority). The 32 MiB ceiling stays for the live tier.

REJECTED: raising the ceiling (capacity, not correctness — any finite bound reproduces the loss, zero reproduces it instantly); ReportedRowsOnScreen arithmetic (refill debt, not departures); disabling pruning per block (unbounded memory); smaller feeds (probability).

THREE DESIGN QUESTIONS the zg3k3.5 implementation must answer before coding (codex verdict on the first plan draft: rework):
1. JOURNAL BUFFER ACCOUNTING — a journal with its own budget is a third loss-capable buffer, which ADR-0075 forbids (both row buffers are user settings, counted). Charge it under the existing helper buffer, prove it non-lossy under a bounded maximum mutation, or amend ADR-0075.
2. RAW vs LOGICAL CURSOR — the fork's raw departure Next is not the durable stream cursor: Go suppresses already-stored closing-screen rows (raw screenDepartedRows vs logical departedRows, observation.go). IntervalEnd must be a logical-cursor snapshot at the marker split, not the journal's latest Next.
3. RESEND ACROSS REFLOW — resend-from-scrollback (rows.go resendFromScrollback) cannot reconstruct records at original indices after width reflow. Choose: resend from the journal, generation-aware resend with stated loss, or accept reflowed resend (conflicts with exact capture).

Also for the plan: the invariant is 'capture BEFORE durable-storage policy is independent of live retention' (blocks remain bounded by outputCapKB/outputEnabled/durable retention/maxResendEnds=64); alt-screen mutations emit nothing but shrink-while-alt-active must emit hidden-primary rows; generation must cross the historyPage wire (contract today promises resize moves nothing — contradiction to resolve); the fork change is a real release (headers, six platform archives, manifest hashes, link verification), not a TrackRow-style wrapper; acceptance stays one 500-block e2e with lower-tier deterministic tests for default/100k/zero.

Status unchanged: blocked on the owner. PR #260 stays draft.

comments.author: prime-root:shady2k@vm-agents:feat/zg3k3-10-scrollback#01a0f988
comments.text:
Owner decision, 2026-10-02 (session 01a0f988, relayed from the owner in Russian): OPTION 2 — decouple durable capture from live retention. Option 1 (raise the 32 MiB ceiling) and option 3 (accept bounded capture with visible incomplete marks) are both rejected. Block lifted; the live tier's bounds stay as shipped.

Two further consultations were run after the blocker was filed; both are recorded in full below. Three consultations now agree on the direction; the open three-way choices from the first round are settled.

Design settled for the zg3k3.5 rework (all three consultations agree):
- the journal and the helper wire queue share ONE byte-credit pool under history.helperBufferMB; overflow takes ADR-0075's existing incomplete-block path; no ADR-0075 change, no hidden internal budget;
- EndRow snapshots the LOGICAL departedRows after closing-screen suppression; the journal's raw Next only delimits what to drain, never EndRow;
- resend comes from an indexed replay ledger of original cells; reclaim needs a prefix-proven ack; reflowed resend is rejected; generation mismatch states loss, never relabels;
- a layout generation is added to the fork history snapshot, HistoryPageView, the helper DTO and the wire schema — the schema's "resize moves nothing" claim is corrected;
- alt-screen: a shrink while alt is active emits hidden primary rows at Resize, once, and not again on return;
- the fork change is a real release: six manifest targets, MANIFEST.json hashes, fetch-verify, make vt-verify-link — not a Go-wrapper-only change;
- acceptance: one 500-block transcript-scroll-budget e2e plus deterministic lower-tier tests (default/100k/zero, same-feed prune, raw-vs-logical at a marker, marker+following bytes, reflow during resend, prune/ED3 stale generations, alt output, hidden-primary shrink, journal drain/release on success/error/close).

Alternatives to the journal were ranked and rejected in consultation #3 (below): a Go durable ring at drain time (too late — a whole 64 KiB sub-feed is processed before the read, and at zero retention Ghostty erases in place via cursorDownScroll/eraseRow, so rows vanish before Go has any readable representation); a history-append/pre-prune hook (blind at zero retention — no_scrollback bypasses both history append and page pruning; hoisted above that branch it IS the primary-boundary hook under another name); raw PTY capture with a second emulator (correct only with a full ordered event log — bytes, resizes, authenticated lifecycle events, fences, settings changes — because lifecycle authority is deliberately outside the PTY per ADR-0024; doubles CPU and still needs boundary capture); explicit scalar prune events (repairs the arithmetic, recovers no contents once one feed's departures exceed the retained tail; carrying contents and indices makes it a journal at the wrong hook); a synchronous boundary callback (correct, but needs a borrowed-row ABI, cannot re-enter non-reentrant Ghostty, pays per-row cgo crossings, needs the same bounded staging and the same six-target release; batching it accumulates rows in the fork — a journal again).

Next: the zg3k3.5 plan is reworked for the departure journal; the work is tracked under nocx-zg3k3.5 (reopened for it).

================================================================================
Consultation #2 — sol (Prime Agent child on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol), 2026-10-02, question: validate the mechanism and answer the three design questions.

VERDICT: NEEDS REWORK, but the direction is sound.

A fork-level monotonic departure odometer plus capture at the primary active-area crossing is the right way to separate durable capture from live retention. A prune must advance retained state, never masquerade as a departure. The 32 MiB live ceiling should stay. The design is not ready until the journal shares the helper's existing bound, resend stops reconstructing old rows from current reflowed history, and live-history cursors gain a layout generation. Marker/block attribution must remain in Go: ADR-0024 decision 1 permits a stream sighting only to locate an already-authenticated event; it cannot create or authenticate the boundary.

1. JOURNAL BUFFER ACCOUNTING — charge it to the existing helper buffer.
The claim "write-ahead for one feed, not a queue behind a slow consumer" is only partly sound. It explains lifetime, not memory or loss. ADR-0075's context is about slow-consumer queues, but its binding decision says both row buffers are the person's settings; AD-10's amendment says the helper buffer shares the helper-wide aggregate; and rows.go:3-16 says the helper has no second buffer and every row/closing screen/marker spends rowBufferBytes.
MaxIngestBytes (64 KiB) bounds input, not cheaply provisionable row mutation: libghostty permits REP up to 65,535 and the geometry allows uint16 dimensions. "Finite" therefore is not a useful non-loss proof for an uncharged allocation. The journal and the logical replay rows it produces must be stages of the existing history.helperBufferMB allocation. Count simultaneous C journal, Go conversion/replay, queued emission, closing-screen, and marker ownership so copying cannot briefly double-spend the bound. On exhaustion, use ADR-0075's existing incomplete-block path. There is no need to change ADR-0075. A separate loss-capable cap would require a new ADR that supersedes it (accepted ADRs are not edited), not a hidden internal budget.
A synchronous, fully drained per-Ingest/per-Resize C journal can remain an implementation detail only if it has no independent lossy cap and its peak is included in that same accounting.

2. RAW VS LOGICAL CURSOR — snapshot departedRows after suppression.
The code confirms the distinction. drainObservationLocked first adds every emulator-reported row to screenDepartedRows (observation.go:438-455), then suppressBoundaryScreenLocked removes the prior block's already-stored closing-screen rows, and only streamRowsLocked advances departedRows (observation.go:485-503). Thus raw journal Next corresponds to the physical/screen departure space, not the durable row-stream space.
The exact marker split is already visible in Session.Ingest: feed the sub-chunk ending at the marker; drain all journal entries caused by that sub-chunk; run closing-screen suppression and emit/retain the kept logical rows; then snapshot departedRows; only after that may sightDrainedFenceLocked/splitObservationAtFenceLocked rebase the next interval or any byte after the marker be fed. Today splitObservationAtFenceLocked stores EndRow: s.departedRows (observation.go:1252-1264), and completion-first seal likewise emits s.departedRows (:534-548). Preserve that ordering. Raw Next may delimit what to drain; it must never be EndRow.

3. RESEND ACROSS REFLOW — resend exact journal-derived logical emissions.
Do not accept reflowed resend. resendFromScrollback currently reads the current HistoryRows tail and labels it from the current departed count (rows.go:679-703). A width change can split/join physical rows, so those cells are not the rows originally assigned those indices. This conflicts with Terminal.DepartedRows' promise to copy a row at departure and with exact durable capture.
Generation-aware resend with stated loss is an honest fallback, but making every disconnected resize a loss wastes rows already captured.
Replace resendFromScrollback's HistoryRows reconstruction with an indexed logical replay ledger populated after Go suppression. Make that ledger and the pending wire FIFO one bounded ownership under history.helperBufferMB, not two copies. Retain sent-but-unconfirmed rows; resend [mark, D) from their original cells, interleaving the existing named dropped ends (still maxResendEnds=64). Reclaim only from an acknowledgement that proves the entire logical prefix durable. The current EarliestIntervalStart/confirmed-mark repair exists because an ack once leapt over a block's missing head; a replay ledger needs a real reclaim watermark or explicit missing ranges, not "retain from the earliest interval forever". If an exact span is absent because the helper buffer overflowed, use ADR-0075's incomplete semantics. A same-generation live-history fallback may be an optimization, never the correctness source; generation mismatch must state loss, never relabel.

4. REQUIREMENTS THE MECHANISM CURRENTLY MISSES
- Alternate screen: alt-screen scrolling emits no durable departures. A row pushed from the hidden primary by a shrink while alt is active does emit, immediately at Resize, and must not be emitted again on return. Current alt_screen_resize_rows_test.go has both required shapes.
- Live-history generation: ADR-0078 says live positions move under reflow/pruning/ED3, while contracts/session.historyPage.schema.json currently says "a resize ... move[s] nothing". Add generation to the fork history snapshot and to the historyPage request/result (and correlated rows carrier). A cursor is (generation, before); mismatch gets an explicit stale/reset answer. Advance generation on every layout-invalidating reflow and destructive retention change; advance floor/generation, not the departure odometer, on prune/ED3. Read floor/head/generation atomically from the fork; stop deriving floor only as screenDepartedRows - HistoryRows.Total.
- Fork release: this changes the public ABI. Land the fork source and generated public headers, build/publish all six manifest targets (Linux amd64/arm64 musl and glibc; Darwin amd64/arm64), update commit/base/patch/tag plus archive and header hashes in MANIFEST.json, fetch-verify them, and run make vt-verify-link (including new-symbol verification). It is not a Go wrapper-only change.
- Acceptance: keep one 500-block transcript-scroll-budget e2e. Add deterministic lower-tier tests for default, 100k (32 MiB binds), and zero (immediate live discard but complete capture), plus same-feed prune, raw-vs-logical suppression at a marker, marker+following bytes, reflow during resend, prune/ED3 stale generations, alt output, hidden-primary shrink, and journal drain/release on success/error/close.

Main risks
- Double count, duplicate, or omission around grow/refill debt, hidden-primary reflow, ED3/reset, and marker sub-feed boundaries.
- C/Go ownership and temporary double copies escaping history.helperBufferMB.
- A scalar confirmation that cannot safely reclaim the exact replay ledger.
- Stale live cursors being silently reused across a generation.
- Shipping mismatched headers/archive ABI on one of the six targets.
- Replacing live-retention loss with helper-buffer loss without surfacing ADR-0075's incomplete state; tests must distinguish the two causes.

================================================================================
Consultation #3 — codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning high, read-only sandbox), 2026-10-02, question: are there OTHER, MORE EFFECTIVE solutions than the fork-ABI departure journal?

## Verdict

**No more effective solution exists; the fork-ABI departure journal stands.**

> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory (Status screen: every project's roadmap and live progress)** — The recorded target is a bounded pull journal at the primary-screen departure boundary, with exact gaps and a shared helper budget. The current source and pinned Ghostty revision confirm that this is the first location common to retained and zero-retention paths.

| Rank / shape | Zero retention | Prune inside feed | Memory | ABI/release | Effort |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| **1. Boundary odometer + pull journal** | Correct | Correct | Shared `history.helperBufferMB` | Fork ABI; six archives | Medium–high |
| 2. Synchronous boundary callback | Correct | Correct | Potentially slightly less staging | Same fork release | High/riskier |
| 3. Raw PTY event log + second emulator | Conditional | Correct if replay is exact | Raw log + second emulator | No fork ABI | Very high |
| 4. Explicit prune-count events | Incorrect | Only sometimes | Small | Fork ABI; six archives | Medium |
| 5. Go ring at drain time | Incorrect | Incorrect | Third buffer | None | Low |
| 6. History-append/pre-prune hook | Incorrect | Partial | Extra staging | Fork ABI; six archives | Medium |

### 1. Go durable ring at drain time

It is already too late. `Session.Ingest` calls `emulator.Ingest(chunk)` and only afterwards calls `drainObservationLocked`; that drain can copy only what `DepartedRows()` survived with ([runtime.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/sessionruntime/runtime.go:1183), [observation.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/sessionruntime/observation.go:423)).

A whole 64 KiB sub-feed is processed before the read. During it Ghostty may repeatedly grow and recycle old pages. At zero retention it does not create history at all: `cursorDownScroll` takes `eraseRow`, shifting the active area in place ([pinned Screen.zig](https://github.com/shady2k/ghostty/blob/1f225ebb5894189aa9e12cf3a371f787e574c5f4/src/terminal/Screen.zig#L920-L1000)). Thus rows can disappear before Go has any readable representation. A Go ring would preserve only already-preserved rows and introduce another loss-capable buffer.

### 2. History-append or pre-prune hook

**A pre-prune hook does not cover zero retention.** Setting zero immediately erases history and sets `no_scrollback` ([scrollback.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/emulator/ghostty/scrollback.go:96), [pinned Terminal.zig](https://github.com/shady2k/ghostty/blob/1f225ebb5894189aa9e12cf3a371f787e574c5f4/src/terminal/Terminal.zig#L460-L472)). Future scrolling follows the in-place erase path, bypassing both history append and page pruning.

With retention enabled, `grow()` may append and then prune or directly recycle the first page ([pinned PageList.zig](https://github.com/shady2k/ghostty/blob/1f225ebb5894189aa9e12cf3a371f787e574c5f4/src/terminal/PageList.zig#L3949-L4106)). A history-append hook could cover that path, but not zero. Moving the hook above the `no_scrollback` branch makes it a **primary-boundary departure hook**—the chosen capture point under another name.

### 3. Raw PTY capture and second emulation

This can be made correct only by recording an ordered event log containing:

- PTY bytes;
- every committed resize and screen transition;
- authenticated lifecycle events and their matching in-band fences;
- settings/reset changes affecting emulation.

Bytes alone are insufficient because lifecycle authority is deliberately outside the PTY, while fences only locate authenticated events in render order ([ADR-0024](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/docs/decisions/0024-authenticated-shell-integration-channel.md:148), [render ordering](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/docs/decisions/0024-authenticated-shell-integration-channel.md:566)).

It doubles emulation CPU, introduces another emulator’s state/memory, and creates replay-divergence and checkpointing work. Unlimited replay scrollback merely relocates the unbounded-memory problem; bounded replay still needs boundary capture. It avoids the six-archive fork release, but loses decisively on memory and effort.

### 4. Explicit page-prune events

A scalar prune count repairs the equation for ordinary bounded growth:

`departures = depth_after - depth_before + pruned_rows`.

It does **not** recover row contents once a single feed creates more departures than the retained tail can hold; terminal sequences can expand far beyond their byte length, and the runtime intentionally leaves that expansion to Ghostty ([runtime.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/sessionruntime/runtime.go:1132)). It also sees no event on the zero-retention `eraseRow` path.

If prune events carry the discarded row contents and monotonic indices, they become a departure journal, but at the wrong, retention-specific hook.

### 5. Cheapest defensible variant: synchronous boundary callback

The only credible alternative is a fork callback invoked before every primary-row discard, delivering the complete borrowed row directly to Go. Existing effect callbacks prove synchronous C→Go callbacks are supported under the terminal lock ([terminal.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/emulator/ghostty/terminal.go:123)).

It still does not beat the journal:

- complete styled rows require a new borrowed-row ABI or serialization;
- Go cannot re-enter non-reentrant Ghostty to read cells during the callback;
- per-row cgo crossings are expensive;
- it still needs bounded staging and exact overflow accounting;
- it incurs the same six-target archive release documented by the pin ([README](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/third_party/libghostty-vt/README.md:71)).

A batched callback reduces crossings only by accumulating rows inside the fork—again, a journal.

## Design conditions that remain mandatory

- Journal plus helper wire queue must share one byte-credit pool under `history.helperBufferMB`; two independently full-sized buffers would violate [ADR-0075](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/docs/decisions/0075-an-overflowing-row-stream-ends-the-block-in-flight-incomplete.md:65).
- Raw departure indices remain distinct from Go’s logical `departedRows`, because closing-screen suppression makes `screenDepartedRows` larger ([runtime.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/sessionruntime/runtime.go:274)).
- Resend must use the indexed replay ledger, not `resendFromScrollback`, which currently reconstructs indices from reflowable retained history ([rows.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/helper/session/rows.go:624)).
- Layout generation must be added to `HistoryPageView`, helper DTO, and wire schema; none currently carries it, and the schema currently claims resize moves nothing ([history_page.go](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/internal/sessionruntime/history_page.go:52), [schema](/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-silver-harbor-4727/contracts/session.historyPage.schema.json:15)).

title: The resend serves original cells from the helper's retained window, and reclaim needs a prefix-proven ack
description:

REOPENED 2026-10-04: the close of 2026-10-04 said "superseded by the upstream reset" - that is wrong; the defect this leaf covers lives in nocx's helper, not the fork journal, and survives the history-erased callback design unchanged (the reviewer's correction).

Problem, verified in the tree: internal/helper/session/rows.go resendFromScrollback (L639) rebuilds the unacknowledged span from the EMULATOR'S LIVE history (t.HistoryRows via ReadDepartedScreen, bounded below by EarliestIntervalStart). Delivered-but-unacked rows are not in the helper's wire FIFO (the owner's decision gives the helper no second buffer), so under the bounded live tier the resend can be defeated by: (a) pruning during a disconnect - rows the live tier dropped cannot be re-read; (b) a width change during a disconnect - reflow serves reflowed rows at the wrong absolute indices.

What it builds:
- the helper keeps delivered rows in its EXISTING bounded buffer (history.helperBufferMB) from emission until an acknowledgement proves the whole logical prefix durable - a real reclaim watermark or explicit missing ranges, not EarliestIntervalStart's retain-forever repair;
- resendFromScrollback's HistoryRows reconstruction is REPLACED: resend serves original cells at their original indices from the helper's retained window, interleaving the named dropped ends (maxResendEnds = 64 unchanged); a reflow or generation mismatch is stated as loss, never relabelled;
- overflow takes ADR-0075's existing path: the block in flight ends incomplete from the named row, rows drop until the next end marker (carried with its own fence), recording resumes at the next command.

DONE WHEN: helper tests show (a) a width change during a disconnected span makes resend serve the ORIGINAL rows at their original indices (reflowed resend rejected), (b) a prune during a disconnected span still serves the emitted rows from the retained window, (c) an ack that leapt over a missing head reclaims nothing it cannot prove, (d) a span absent from the retained window (buffer overflow) is stated as ADR-0075 incomplete loss at its position.

title: Stored-row reads of many different large blocks can still overflow the 64-frame response queue and tear the connection
description:
The renderer can still exhaust the transport's reserved response queue with stored-row reads of DIFFERENT large blocks — the 2648f1b4 coalesce fixes duplicate reads of ONE entry only.

Mechanism (code-confirmed 2026-10-04, nocx-zg3k3.5 PR #263; trace 8f61a46e7e45a2f9f2d1eb5a15bc378c, round-3 chromium-2):
1. frontend/src/terminal-content.ts subscribes `refreshBlockRows` to BOTH `block.grew` (line 4576) and `block.closed` (4552); each fires `_refreshBlockRows(entryId)` → `blockRowsForEntry` → a FULL `ledger.artifact` read of the block.
2. After a backend restart the renderer re-receives grew/closed for every stored block. N blocks → up to N concurrent full-artifact reads.
3. The server caps only HANDLERS (ledger.get/artifact ride the content-queue, depth 8), not the per-connection RESPONSE queue: `internal/transport/outbound` respQueue = 64 frames, shared 32 MiB process budget; overflow → `overflowResponse()` → `c.Close()` (the connection the server itself tears down).

Measured: one 5000-row artifact = 307,891 B body, 353,052 B JSON-RPC envelope. 64 of those ≈ 21.55 MiB — inside the 32 MiB budget but the queue is 64 FRAMES, so 64 large responses overflow by count even below the byte budget. A history of several long commands (each ~350 KB) or 500 modest blocks (round-1 'measures 500 blocks', trace 65db4170…) fills the 64-frame queue the same way the single-block duplicate burst did.

title: After clear, a person can reveal the cards the clear boundary hid, in their own view only
description:
After `clear` in a shell-integrated session, the cards before it are hidden from an ordinary
read, and nothing lets a person see them again.

## What exists

`clear` inside an authenticated interval records a clear boundary in the durable record
(`RecordClearBoundary`, nocx-2v80t.3.17): a cursor a reader applies, not a mark on the
entries, so the record never deletes (ADR-0078 decision 2). The store answers only the
"no reveal requested" case (`internal/content/ledger_sqlite.go`), so the hidden cards are
kept and unreachable.

## Why it is filed now

The owner's rule of 2026-09-21 — the record never deletes, `clear` bounds what is SHOWN,
revealing is explicit, per client and per view — used to be carried by the live-scrollback
tasks nocx-zg3k3.10.3 and .10.4. On 2026-10-01 the owner took it out of the live tier ("with
no shell integration, on clear we pass ghostty's view as it is"), which left the durable
tier's reveal tracked nowhere. Recorded in ADR-0078.

## What done would look like

- After `clear`, the transcript shows a visible row where the hidden cards were, with a way
  to reveal them; revealing shows them in that client and view only, does not mutate the
  session, and does not change what a client attaching later sees by default.
- A reveal whose cards were evicted by retention says so, never an empty success.
- Disproved if the hidden cards can only be reached by reading the store.

## Left out

The live tier (the emulator's own scrollback), which shows the emulator's view as it is.

Review at the next milestone's planning (0.7): whether this joins it.

title: The emulator reads a departed row once per row rather than once per column, so terminal output is taken in at more than 0.8 MiB/s
description:
Measured 2026-09-29 by the ingest budget (nocx-zg3k3.5.8, internal/sessionruntime/ingest_budget_test.go, run branch feat/zg3k3-5-unwatched-output at 862910f50): the helper takes terminal output at ~0.82 MiB/s at 120x40 -- a 4 MiB feed costs ~4.9 s, 8.4M allocations and 225 MB allocated per MiB. Cause, from the profile: internal/emulator/ghostty/terminal.go captureDepartedLocked (~line 833) reads each departed row through rowAt -> readCell, which resolves C.nocxGridRefAt once per COLUMN, and each history resolution walks the page list. readGrapheme allocates a maxGraphemeCodepoints buffer per text cell (32.9% of allocated bytes). - captureDepartedLocked resolves each departed history row once (nocxGridResolveCount per departed row == 1), asserted by a test.

title: Readers of the encrypted content store run alongside a writer again, because a per-file I/O lock outside the adiantum VFS replaces the one-connection pool
description:
The encrypted content store runs on one connection (ADR-0043, maxOpenConns = 1) because the adiantum VFS rewrites the 4096-byte cipher block holding the tail of the previous, committed WAL frame on every append, and a reader on another handle can read that block mid-rewrite. Since the one-transaction-per-lifecycle-frame design of nocx-zg3k3.5.11 (ADR-0077), a frame holds that single connection from its first write to its commit, so every read in nocx -- history, search, a window opening -- waits for the frame's whole hold. ADR-0043 names the end state: a shared I/O lock OUTSIDE the encrypting VFS, one mutex per physical file, held across a whole encrypted ReadAt/WriteAt rather than around the OS calls inside it. Transactions then stay concurrent (WAL readers alongside the writer) and only the byte-level rewrite of one cipher block is serialized.

Owner's decision, 2026-09-30: this is filed as its own task; the stage nocx-zg3k3.5 keeps one connection with a bounded frame hold.

The upstream report nocx-8xseo was never sent: no matching issue in ncruces/go-sqlite3 by two searches on 2026-09-30, and releases v0.35.3..v0.35.6 carry no fix (nocx pins v0.35.2). Send it first; if upstream fixes the VFS, this task becomes a driver upgrade plus the gates below.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The ADR-0043 reproducer (one writer, 16 readers, vfs=adiantum, WAL) with the pool raised to 16 and NO lock fails with 'database disk image is malformed'; with the lock it passes the same profile, replicated, under -race in the CI container within the package timeout.
- The pool is raised above one; TestThePoolIsOneConnection is replaced by a gate that fails by name when the lock is removed or bypassed.
- While a lifecycle frame holds a write transaction, a concurrent Entry/history read completes without waiting for the frame's commit (measured, with the numbers in the task).
- A new ADR supersedes ADR-0043's decision; ADR-0043 is not edited; its INDEX.md row says what superseded it.
- nocx-8xseo is sent or closed with the upstream link.

## Out
- Two nocx processes on one database file (the cross-process case ADR-0043 flags; nocx-amst3).

title: A lifecycle frame is written as two writes, so a frame another writer sends on the same descriptor can land inside it and break the reader's framing
description:
A repair the merge of stage nocx-zg3k3.5 (PR #255) waits on — not a finding.

What happens: CI run 36757852925 (head eb9ceade0), job ci-backend (with-secret-service), fails TestBashNestedChildDomainSuFallback at nested_domain_test.go:1125: "timed out waiting for late fallback child frame rejection; rejected=0 order=[... dom-test domain_activated dom-test complete]". Idle, the test passes 30 of 30 on the branch.

Cause: lifecyclecodec.Encode (internal/lifecyclecodec/codec.go) puts one frame on the wire as TWO Write calls, the 4-byte length header and then the body. The test's injectLateChildFrame encodes its late child frame onto the same socketpair the parent bash is still writing its own frames to (complete, then prompt_ready), right after the fallback child exits. When the shell's frame lands between the injected header and its body, the fake kernel reads a body that is not one frame, loses framing, and its read loop ends — so the rejection is never counted and prompt_ready never appears, which is exactly the order CI printed. Encode and the test are the same on main; the branch did not bring it.

What should happen: a frame reaches its descriptor in one write, so a second writer on the same descriptor can never land inside it — in the test and for any product caller that shares a descriptor.

## DONE WHEN

A test in internal/lifecyclecodec asserts Encode hands its writer exactly one Write holding header and body together; it is red on the current code and green after. TestBashNestedChildDomainSuFallback and its stillborn twins stay green.

Falsified if Encode ever splits one frame across more than one Write.

title: Resizing a valid wide C terminal clamps PageList row capacity instead of overflowing

A regression probe for nocx-zg3k3.5.14 found a separate valid-input failure in the Ghostty fork. `ghostty_terminal_new` and `ghostty_terminal_resize` accept any nonzero `uint16_t` width/height (include/ghostty/vt/terminal.h:2028-2053; c/terminal.zig:833-838,1503-1523). title: The stage review's findings on the loss wording, the ingest budget and the frame-bound test are fixed
description:
Codex review of feat/zg3k3-5-unwatched-output at b19351494, 2026-09-29 (stage acceptance, one round). Three majors, each a repair the stage's merge waits on:

1. frontend/src/scrollback/block-rows.ts ~175 presents lostRows as an exact count of rows pruned from scrollback. The runtime contract lets it be a symbolic count of struck feeds (one feed may lose hundreds of rows and count 1), and the store also adds bridge drops to it. So a card can say one row was lost, and attribute a bridge loss to pruning.
2. internal/sessionruntime/ingest_budget_test.go ~96 gates a test RowStream that re-implements the helper's split/encode loop, so a regression in internal/helper/session/rows.go (the shipped pump) leaves the gate unchanged.
3. internal/transport/ws_block_rows_bounds_test.go ~470 asserts no frame exceeds 32 rows without first proving a batch larger than 32 reached the pump; at 120x40 and 200x50 the observed maxima were 29 and 19, so removing the production split could stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The card never states a row count it does not know: a loss counted in feeds or of unknown size is worded as such, each cause keeps its own words, and a test pins a one-feed loss that is not rendered as '1 row'. If the store conflates bridge drops with scrollback pruning, they are separated or worded as one honest cause.
- The ingest budget gates the production pump code (internal/helper/session), or the pump's encoding moves where both can call it -- one implementation; a hand-planted extra copy in the production pump turns the gate red.
- The bounds test asserts, as a precondition, that at least one pump batch exceeded 32 rows at each size (or forces one deterministically), and removing the production split turns it red at every size.
